properties.name: A proof can state what it really does: a contradiction (falsum) reads false, a case split is checked exhaustive, a supposition has its own kind, and a cited theorem (verified or not) differs from an axiom
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-18, choosing D (the rest) of the build list
properties.statement:
From the 2026-10-17/18 proof trials:
1. A falsum statement (a contradiction derived inside a reductio) reads as false, not "holds".
2. A proof-by-cases step can name its cases, and reflow2 says whether they are declared exhaustive. The exhaustiveness itself is the owner's or a checker's word.
3. statement_kind gains a value for a supposition or hypothesis.
4. A theorem cited from elsewhere reads "cited, not proved here", distinct from an axiom or definition. A citation recalled but not checked against its source reads "cited, unverified", never plain "holds".
5. The design-a-proof skill gains a recipe for each of these, and agrees with the tools.
The schema stamp is expected to move: every seat upgrades together.
